params.body:
Portal reads policy versions in the digest form, and signs in it once the gateway reads it.

The gateway (control, policy-digest) accepts a version signed on a short head `{type, iss, version, prev, iat, body_hash}` that names the body `{agents, systems, change}` by hash, so a YubiKey signs any version; the whole-payload form stopped at about a kilobyte.

- `PolicyLog::decode` reads both forms: the head and body decode strictly, the body must hash to `body_hash`, the signature is checked over what it covers. `check`, `keep` and the repair check (`notTheRepairDrafted`) work on the decoded claims, so the rules are unchanged.
- `PolicyLog::served` keeps the `formats` the gateway reports through Elixir's `controlGrants`; `digestForm()` says whether to sign in the new form.
- The passkey repair (`PolicyApproval`) signs the head with Portal's key through `Capability::signBytes` (split out of `sign`, same KMS or seed path).
- The phone (`SignOnKey`) is offered the head instead of the whole payload; Portal keeps the body with the offer and puts it back between head and signature when the token returns. The app's checks are unchanged: a policy offer is still a `policy-version` without an issuer.
- Before the gateway lists `digest`, everything is signed and read as before.

Tests: a digest version kept, its body held to its head, a forged head and a smuggled field refused, both forms on one chain; the passkey repair and the phone in the digest form. Full suite 745 of 746 (the one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which needs a real checkout's build stamp), PHPStan and Pint clean.
